targets.note: one decade is enough: the question is whether the engine reproduces the free value at all. Confirmed by the person at ad38bb0, so the value does not move at this revision -- what moved is that it stopped being this agent's E5 assumption

estimation.note: the weighted least squares the vocabulary declares, run by the backend and citing the contract in its own output. What is compared here is the fit range, which is the part of the estimator a run can fail to honour by stopping early

numbers.name: temperature
numbers.note: the operator's thermometer reading of the room. It is not established to be the sample's temperature -- see the gap

numbers.name: viscosity
numbers.note: pure water. The entry's validity runs 288 to 298 K, and the temperature above is inside it

numbers.name: bead_diameter
numbers.note: the tracer the question is about, measured directly by the operator on 2026-09-19 with a coefficient of variation no greater than 2 per cent. Cited as kb: rather than calibration: -- the grade is E2 either way, but this agent holds no calibration and the citation is what puts the entry in kb_refs

numbers.name: n_particles
numbers.note: tracers per box. Non-interacting, so the ensemble is a statistics knob rather than a physical density -- but the box still has to hold them dilutely (A3)

numbers.name: integration_timestep_planned
numbers.note: ten steps per saved frame, so every frame lands on a step. Well inside A1's ceiling, which A1 set from the diffusive time rather than from the sampling

numbers.name: total_simulated_time_planned
numbers.note: two decades above the statistical floor. A decade was not enough: it made the record as long as the window, and then the longest lag carries one displacement per tracer

numbers.name: save_interval_planned
numbers.note: upper bound. Saving more often costs storage, which is A5's, not A4's

numbers.name: max_lag_time_planned
numbers.note: the window the estimator is evaluated over, set below tau_d so the free regime is what is sampled. Held at the tenth of tau_d revision 1 used: at the new tau_d the old 2 s would have been under one per cent of it, which samples only the shortest lags. tracer_diffusivity is window_required, so this travels with the plan as a condition. A4 constrains it

numbers.name: box_length
numbers.note: the binding bound here: dilution costs a hundred microns, images only nine

numbers.name: target_relative_error
numbers.note: ten per cent, which is well inside the one decade the goal asks for

numbers.name: intercept_sigma_max
numbers.note: how far the MSD fit's intercept may sit from zero, in standard errors of the BLOCK-RESAMPLED uncertainty and not the fit's own. The fit treats correlated MSD points as independent and quotes an error about 36x too small (measured over 32 seeds), so the same criterion against the fit's error would refuse a sound run: run-20260920-002 reads 6.5 sigma there and 2.0 sigma here

numbers.name: diffusivity_predicted
numbers.note: bulk Stokes-Einstein: sphere, bulk, no slip. Those assumptions stay in the value. The relation is the librarian's (kb:tracer_diffusivity_expected), not a second one -- recomputing a quantity the store holds is a detour, and citing it is what gets the one name. This is the expectation the run is checked against, and the engine derives its own from the same bath rather than being handed this number

numbers.name: relative_standard_error
numbers.note: the block standard error over the estimate: 50 blocks of 20 tracers refitted with the same estimator. The tracers do not interact here, so the blocks are independent by construction. The fit's own relative error is in the run record and is about 36 times smaller than the spread this configuration actually shows

numbers.name: decades_from_prediction
numbers.note: log10 of the fitted diffusivity over the plan's Stokes-Einstein expectation, in absolute value so that a factor low fails the same way as a factor high. Not a computed: number: check 17's formula language has + - * / ** and no logarithm, so a decade count cannot be written as an arithmetic the validator can redo

numbers.name: intercept_in_block_sigma
numbers.note: the MSD fit's intercept over the block-resampled error on it. This backend has no localisation error for a free intercept to absorb, so a nonzero one is the window and not the physics

numbers.name: window_half_disagreement
numbers.note: log10 of the diffusivity fitted over the first half of the lag range against the second, in absolute value. It is what separates converged from precise: a fit reaching past the free regime disagrees with itself across the window while each half stays tight, and neither error bar can report that because every block spans the same lags

numbers.name: total_simulated_time_actual
numbers.note: steps_taken * dt, read off an integer step count rather than accumulated. Summing dt ten thousand times gives 19.999999999999794 against a planned end of 20 s, and a comparison at a boundary is a decision rather than a measurement

numbers.name: max_step_displacement
numbers.note: the largest single-step displacement any tracer took, which is what the divergence criterion watches

numbers.name: integration_timestep_actual
numbers.note: the timestep the run actually integrated at, as simulated time over steps taken

numbers.name: save_interval_actual
numbers.note: the interval frames actually landed at, as simulated time over saved intervals

numbers.name: max_lag_time_actual
numbers.note: the longest lag the estimator actually fitted. It is shorter than the plan's window whenever the record ended early, which is the case the estimator's own window bound cannot see from inside

assumptions.statement: One thousand tracers is a round ensemble that makes the statistics cheap and keeps the cube root exact at ten per edge. Nothing physical picks this number.
assumptions.falsifier: a statistics interval this ensemble cannot satisfy inside budget replaces it

assumptions.statement: The fit window sits below the diffusive time so the free regime is what is sampled, at the same tenth of it revision 1 chose. The exact upper end is an estimate until A4 constrains it.
assumptions.falsifier: an A4 interval that excludes this value replaces it

assumptions.statement: A ten per cent statistical error needs of order one hundred independent samples, from the square-root scaling of an ensemble mean. The target is set at ten per cent rather than at the goal's full decade so that the statistical error is not what decides the decade.
assumptions.falsifier: a seed-to-seed spread wider than ten per cent at this sample count retires the prefactor and raises the floor

assumptions.statement: Three standard errors is a guard against a gross short-lag failure, not a test of bias, and it is set from the asymmetry rather than from any observation: a false refusal costs one re-run of a job sitting far under budget, while a false acceptance puts a biased number into a graded card. IT CANNOT DETECT AN ARTIFACT, and saying so is the point -- a systematic short-lag error shows in the MEAN over runs while a fluctuation shows in a single one, and no threshold on a single run's intercept separates them. Tight refuses good runs at the fluctuation rate; loose misses a small artifact. The test that catches an artifact is that the mean intercept over an ensemble of runs is consistent with zero, which needs a campaign and is not a criterion one plan can carry.
assumptions.falsifier: a campaign whose mean intercept is inconsistent with zero, which would show this guard passing runs it cannot judge

kb_refs.claim: The laboratory's ambient temperature is 20 degrees Celsius, read off a thermometer by the operator. It is a reading and not a setpoint, and it is the room's rather than the sample's.
The particles in the bottle in use have a diameter of 5 micrometres, with a coefficient of variation no greater than 2 per cent, measured directly by the operator on 2026-09-19.
Dynamic viscosity of pure water near 293 K is of order one millipascal second, and it changes by roughly two percent per kelvin in that neighbourhood.
